questions.q: What is the real purpose of the Plan activity in the Service Value Chain?
options: To ensure a shared understanding of vision, current status, and improvement direction across the four dimensions of service management
To write code that builds new service components
To resolve individual incidents reported by users
To negotiate contracts directly with external suppliers
questions.explain: Plan's stated purpose in ITIL 4 is exactly this shared-understanding-and-direction role, drawing on input from Engage and Improve.

questions.q: Why is Improve not accurately described as a single improvement project?
options: Because the Improve activity only runs once a year during budget planning
Because it is a standing activity that runs continuously across every other value chain activity, not a one-time initiative
Because ITIL 4 does not define Improve as a value chain activity
Because only the Continual Improvement practice performs improvement work
questions.explain: Improve is one of the six Service Value Chain activities, and it is active at all times inside every other activity, not scoped to one project.

questions.q: Which group of stakeholders does the Engage activity deal with?
options: Only paying customers, never internal staff
Only the IT department's own staff
Users, customers, suppliers, partners, and other internal stakeholders
Only software vendors under contract
questions.explain: Engage's purpose covers good relationships and understanding of needs across all stakeholders, not just one group.

questions.q: Why is it a mistake to picture the six Service Value Chain activities as steps performed strictly in order?
options: Because only three of the six activities are ever used in a given organization
Because ITIL 4 requires activities to run in alphabetical order
Because the Service Value Chain has no connection to inputs and outputs
Because all six activities are active at all times in every organization, connected by flows of inputs and outputs rather than a sequence number
questions.explain: ITIL 4 is explicit that the Service Value Chain's activities aren't a fixed pipeline; they're connected by inputs and outputs that can flow in many directions.

questions.q: In the report-request example in this lesson, what does Improve contribute while Engage and Plan handle the specific request?
options: It watches the request-to-decision process itself, turning a repeating pattern of similar requests into a proposal to fix the underlying process
It replaces the need for Engage to capture the request at all
It makes the final decision on whether the report gets built
It only activates after Design & transition finishes its work
questions.explain: Improve runs continuously in the background, looking for patterns worth fixing at the process level, not just resolving the one request.
